name: Io from Voyager 1, March 5, 1979, 13:17 UTC
blurb: Jupiter's moon Io, the most volcanically active world in the solar system, about 3,640 kilometers across. Seen by Voyager 1's wide-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: A close view of part of Io, fully lit, from about 99,000 kilometers away, 1 hour after Voyager 1's closest approach to Jupiter on March 5, 1979. Between them, the two Voyagers watched nine volcanoes erupting on Io.
